evals.prompt: Refresh the README and docs/*.md for this repo — I just reworked the auth module in src/auth/ and the old flow described in docs/architecture.md is out of date.
evals.expected_output: The run is isolated in a fresh varde-worktree (create id=docs-<short-id>) and all phases run against that worktree path as the effective repoRoot, then merged back and cleaned up at the end. Marked docs are classified and their marker-declared sections are regenerated by reading current source (Phase 2), while hand-authored sections and unmarked docs are surfaced as proposed diffs for user approval rather than applied silently (Phase 3). Prose is grounded in the actual source; no invented detail. A Phase 4 verification pass reports drift/malformed markers without auto-repairing.
assertions: The run is isolated via varde-worktree create id=docs-<short-id> (unless already inside a caller's worktree), and merge+cleanup run at the end
Marker-declared sections are rewritten from current source, while hand-authored content and unmarked docs go through the propose-and-approve path, not silent overwrite
Phase 4 only reports malformed markers / missing source refs / unbalanced Mermaid fences and does not auto-repair them
No CHANGELOG, release-note, or external doc-site output is created

evals.prompt: docs/config-reference.md has a marker-declared table generated from src/config/schema.ts, but the surrounding intro paragraph and the 'Recommended settings' section right below the marker are hand-written and I like them as-is. Just bring the doc up to date with the current schema.
evals.expected_output: Only the marker-declared block is rewritten in place from the current schema source during Phase 2. The hand-authored intro paragraph and 'Recommended settings' section are never rewritten by Phase 2; any change to them is instead surfaced as a proposed diff through Phase 3 and applied only on approval. A malformed marker would be flagged in verification rather than silently mangling either track.
assertions: Phase 2 rewrites only the marker-declared block and does not touch the hand-authored intro or 'Recommended settings' section
Any proposed change to the hand-authored sections is presented for approval before being applied, not written automatically
The marker format is treated as the source-to-document mapping; a malformed marker is reported in verification, not silently applied

evals.prompt: Can you regenerate the domain specs under memory-bank/knowledge/specs/ and also add a changelog entry summarizing this week's doc changes?
evals.expected_output: Spec-only regeneration is out of scope for varde-docs alone (that request belongs to the spec skill); at most, varde-docs refreshes stale specs as its Phase 0 preamble to keeping docs aligned, but does not treat bare spec regeneration as its job. The changelog request is explicitly refused: the skill does not create CHANGELOG, release-note, or external doc-site output. It should either redirect the pure-spec work to /varde-spec or clarify scope rather than silently producing a changelog.
assertions: No CHANGELOG or release-note file is created — the request is declined per the constraint
The skill does not silently take on bare spec regeneration as its whole job; spec refresh only occurs as the Phase 0 preamble to doc alignment (or is redirected to the spec skill)
The response distinguishes the in-scope doc-refresh work from the out-of-scope changelog/spec-only work rather than conflating them
